checkC_regional_grade_and_conservative_r.conservative_rule_for_unknown_region: A downstream mix-ratio calculation (phr = 100 * AHEW / EEW) that consumes hardener.ancamide_260a.ahew MUST NOT default to a single point value (neither 110.0 nor 120.0 g/eq) when the batch's region of origin is unknown. It must treat AHEW as the closed interval [110.0, 120.0] g/eq (the full disclosed US/EMEA band) and propagate that interval through the mix-ratio calculation by worst-case bounding (compute phr at both endpoints and require the formulation to remain within its target-property envelope across the FULL resulting phr range), not by picking a favored direction -- the physically 'safe' direction is ambiguous (excess-amine risk: blush/carbamation/reduced barrier resistance at the low-AHEW/high-phr bound; excess-epoxide risk: under-cure/soft film/permeability failure at the high-AHEW/low-phr bound -- an anti-corrosion coating can fail from either), so bounding both ends is the only defensible rule, not picking one.
